subject: jungle soldier
title: A Soldier Kept Fighting World War II Until 1974. One Order Ended It

scenes.text: One soldier kept fighting World War Two until 1974.
In December 1944, Japan sent Hiroo Onoda to Lubang Island in the Philippines with an order: never surrender.
The war ended eight months later. Leaflets dropped from planes said so. He decided they were an enemy trick.
So he stayed in the jungle for nearly 29 years, while the three men with him surrendered or were killed.
In 1974, a young Japanese traveler tracked him down. Onoda still refused to quit without orders.
So his old commander, by then a bookseller, was flown in to relieve him. Onoda handed over his sword and a working rifle.

description:
A Japanese soldier kept fighting the Second World War until 1974.
Lieutenant Hiroo Onoda was sent to Lubang Island in the Philippines in December 1944 with orders never to surrender or take his own life. When Japan surrendered in August 1945 he and three other soldiers dismissed the leaflets announcing it as Allied propaganda and went on fighting a guerrilla war from the jungle. One of the men surrendered in 1950; the other two were killed in clashes in the 1950s and in 1972. Up to 30 islanders are said to have been killed in the group's raids over the years. In February 1974 a Japanese traveller, Norio Suzuki, found Onoda, who said he would stop only on orders from a superior. His former commanding officer, Major Yoshimi Taniguchi, by then a bookseller, flew to Lubang and formally relieved him in March 1974. Onoda handed over his sword, a working rifle, about 500 rounds of ammunition and several grenades, and was pardoned by President Ferdinand Marcos. He died in Tokyo in January 2014, aged 91.
Would you have believed the leaflets? Comment below.
first_comment: The traveler who found him said he was looking for Onoda, a panda and the Abominable Snowman, in that order. Would you have believed the leaflets?
